tasks.short: Observe experiments and record production and test data

steps.what: Monitor and observe experiments for relevant changes and test conditions
Record production and test data for research personnel evaluation

tasks.design: Configure experiment-specific entry fields in the laboratory records system {OTHER} to reuse identifiers and show missing values while the technician records observations. Retain physical monitoring and record verification; later database transfer is a separate task and is not also saved here.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recording repeats experiment context and allows avoidable omissions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native validated forms can reuse context while keeping source observations explicit.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected experimental behaviour and notes that do not fit fixed fields.
tasks.human_edge: Notice meaningful changes and distinguish an observation from an interpretation.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less repeated context entry; experimental attention remains unchanged.

reach.learn: Protocol deviations and traceable observation records

evidence.claim: Castor EDC provides conditional forms and an audit trail, supporting validated entry capability rather than automatic experimental observation.

assumptions: Boundary is experiment observation and original record creation, excluding experiment setup and subsequent duplicate database entry. The original observation is captured once and reused downstream.

Technician produces experiment/sample IDs, protocol revision, observation time, units, measured value or factual observation and deviation context in s2; its 24 remaining hours include original capture, checking and free-text exceptions. Instrument is the existing producer of instrument results, which remain linked to its source record; missing data are manually clarified, never inferred.

Study lead supplies protocol and required fields through existing protocol work. Test native laboratory forms first; three focal and two laboratory-system-owner upkeep hours cover form changes and checks. Existing forms already in use earn no new saving.
research_questions: Does context reuse reduce entry time without losing unexpected experimental observations?

already_counted.description: Original observation capture and record verification

approvals.approved_version: Exact experiment/sample, protocol revision, timestamp, values/units, observation wording and source links; corrections require renewed record confirmation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=70+24=94, gross=6, upkeep=3, net=3. High assumes 20% less repeated context entry in the recording step. Low assumes bespoke observations retain all recording time plus upkeep. Monitoring and original factual capture retain time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Examine animals and specimens for disease or problems

steps.what: Examine animals and specimens to detect disease signs or other problems

tasks.design: Retain direct examination under the relevant protocol. Existing reference guidance in {DOCS} supports observation, but sample tracking or report software does not establish disease-detection coverage.
tasks.previous_blocker: Problems must be recognised from actual organisms and specimens.
tasks.enabler_now: No validated examination replacement is supplied.
tasks.still_hard: Subtle abnormalities and unexpected conditions needing escalation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise observations that require scientific or veterinary review.
tasks.altitude: Examination effort and professional boundaries remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Direct animal and specimen examination retains time; the digest's record systems do not demonstrate general disease-detection automation.

assumptions: Boundary is technician examination and detection of concerns, excluding separate recording, diagnosis by authorised professionals and treatment.
Technician produces observations within the fully retained step; no structured disease flag or complete imaging dataset is assumed.
Use native protocol access first. No introduced examination system adds upkeep.
research_questions: Which abnormalities require specialist examination rather than a routine technician observation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Physical examination and recognition retain full time; no administrative share is added.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Verify source data identity, units and destination database fields
Input the verified data batch into the database staging area
Reconcile staged database data and confirm the exact committed batch

tasks.design: Test native import into the laboratory database {OTHER} using explicit sample, method and unit mappings. Stage records with source references, reject duplicates or invalid mappings and let the technician reconcile and commit the exact batch; no model changes scientific values.
tasks.previous_blocker: Verified instrument or experiment records are re-keyed into a second database.
tasks.enabler_now: Native import and validation rules can transfer explicit structured records.
tasks.still_hard: Identifier mismatches, revised methods, unit conversions and corrected results.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise a valid-looking value that belongs to the wrong sample or method.
tasks.altitude: Less repeat entry; data identity and release responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Reconcile analytical records and source provenance
reach.learn: Method versions, units and correction audit trails

evidence.claim: SampleManager LIMS tracks barcoded samples, assigns tests and logs changes; Castor EDC provides conditional forms and audit trails. These support structured laboratory record capability, not this saving estimate.
Native staging import that removes repeat database entry is an E1 model-knowledge design scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is secondary database entry from existing checked source records, excluding original experimental observation and record capture. The monitor-and-record task produces that evidence once; no double saving of its capture time is claimed.

Technician produces verified sample/experiment IDs, method and revision, timestamp, value/unit, source reference, correction status and destination mapping in s1; all 30 hours retain verification and manual mapping capture. Instrument or original record author is the existing source producer. Paper-only, ambiguous or unsupported records use manually checked entry rather than uncounted extraction.

Laboratory system owner maintains the field specification and mapping; allow three other-role upkeep hours. Test native import first; six focal upkeep hours cover schema changes and exceptions. Existing imports or instrument runtime earn no new saving.
research_questions: Can sample identity, method revision and corrected results be preserved through native import with less total effort?

already_counted.description: Batch reconciliation, exceptions and commit approval

approvals.approved_version: Exact batch hash, source references, sample/method IDs, values/units, corrections and destination schema revision; edits void commit approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+0+25=55, gross=45, upkeep=6, net=39. High requires presently manual repeat entry and compatible structured sources. Low assumes paper-only or unsupported records retain full entry plus upkeep. Original collection, verification and final reconciliation retain time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Monitor laboratory work and inspect adherence to the current procedures
Evaluate laboratory compliance concerns and escalate departures from set standards

tasks.design: Retain direct monitoring and evaluation of laboratory practice. Current procedures in {DOCS} support checking; database validation and audit trails do not show that physical procedures were actually followed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Record completeness cannot establish actual laboratory conduct.
tasks.enabler_now: No validated replacement for practice observation is established.
tasks.still_hard: Subtle departures, undocumented exceptions and context-dependent escalation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a plausible record conflicts with observed practice.
tasks.altitude: Compliance monitoring and escalation effort remain unchanged.

reach.task: Investigate discrepancies between records and laboratory practice

evidence.claim: Laboratory record systems support traceability but do not replace observing compliance with procedures; retaining this work is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is practice monitoring and immediate escalation, excluding experimental observations already owned by that task and separate deviation report production. Shared observations are assigned once in roll-up.

Technician produces observed practice and deviation concerns within retained steps. Procedure owner supplies existing current standards; no machine-readable compliance flag or full monitoring coverage is assumed.
Use native procedure access first. Unchanged monitoring creates no upkeep; accreditation and regulated-process requirements must be confirmed locally.
research_questions: Which practices must be observed directly despite complete electronic records?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=60+40=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Observation, compliance judgement and escalation retain full time; database entry savings remain in the separate task.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repeated context entry and secondary database transcription where present; retain experimental attention, specimen examination and practice monitoring.
reach: Reconcile source provenance with quality control analysts
Clarify experimental evidence with medical scientists
skills_to_grow: Distinguishing record completeness from actual compliance
role.ambitious_version: A biological technician with traceable experimental records and less repeat entry who retains careful observation of organisms and laboratory work.
